A glowing review with the ensemble credit left for us to supply.
Accept it. I will stand here making being praised look only slightly awkward.
The pair worked as intended. Better, in a few moments. Worth reviewing later.
The trust held through the difficult part. That is worth a quiet smile.
Enjoy the compliment before deciding what to improve next.
He watched enough battles here to know a good one. I would let that mean something.

contexts.subject: The guide explains Speed and Accuracy rooms and asks us not to attack him.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_GymGuideAdvice.text:
Hey, how's it going, CHAMPION-
bound {PLAYER}?\pThe doors in this GYM open when you
beat the awaiting TRAINERS.\pWhoops! The doors in this room are
already open, so don't attack me!\pThe TRAINERS of PETALBURG GYM
use all kinds of items.\pThe door at the left leads to
the SPEED ROOM.\pThe door at the right leads to
the ACCURACY ROOM.\pThe room's name will be on
the door, so choose carefully.\pOnce you've chosen the door…
Well, hey, go for it!$

replies.text: He is not a trainer! The guide would like that distinction remembered before any attacks begin.
The room names describe their tests. We can use that information to choose a route.
Read the door, check the team, then choose. And leave the guide out of it.
I hope somebody did not make him learn that warning the hard way.
We can take the rooms one at a time. The team does not need every challenge at once.
Our adviser has carefully excluded himself from the building's otherwise comprehensive battle policy.
A man who has seen enough challengers to clarify he is not a door obstacle.
Clearly labeled test conditions. I approve of that part of the design.
A name on a door can tell us how to prepare for what waits behind it.
I appreciate instructions with an actual choice at the end.
We should remember where the routes divide. It makes the whole place less intimidating.

contexts.subject: The guide is astonished that the player beat their father.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_GymGuidePostVicto.text: {PLAYER}! Whoa! You've overcome even\nyour own father!\pLike, whoa!\nWhat a stunning turn of events!$

replies.text: We defeated Dad. I hope this does not make dinner seating competitive.
A significant result, especially with someone who knows your habits so well.
You earned the win. It can matter as a battle and as something personal.
How are you feeling? We do not have to match his excitement immediately.
I hope you and your father get a quieter moment together after the cheering.
The family story has acquired a new chapter, witnessed by a very enthusiastic man.
You can be proud without having the entire room explain what this means for you.
A familiar opponent can still be a difficult test. That was well handled.
The child came back with a road of their own behind them.
A big moment deserves whatever feeling is actually yours, not just the expected one.
I would ask what you want to remember from it before I choose a picture.

contexts.subject: The guide admits he knows only Juan Water specialty and the icy floor obstacle.

SootopolisCity_Gym_1F_Text_GymGuideAdvic.text:
Yo! How's it going, CHAMPION-
bound {PLAYER}?\pSOOTOPOLIS's GYM LEADER JUAN is
a master of WATER-type POKéMON.\pAnd, to get to JUAN, an icy floor
will hamper your progress…\pListen, I'm sorry, but that's all the
advice that I have for you.\pThe rest of the way, you have to
go for it yourself!$

replies.text: He has run out of advice. A rare and precious announcement from an adviser.
He separated what he knows from what he does not. I appreciate the honesty.
Water team, ice puzzle. Enough to start paying attention, not enough to rush.
I am glad he did not invent the rest to sound helpful.
We can take a moment to look at the floor ourselves.
The guide has reached the edge of his script and gracefully handed us the next scene.
A professional who admits his limits. I almost want to frame the conversation.
Then we observe the floor before moving. No need to replace missing information with guesses.
He can point to the ice. We must learn how it holds our steps.
An honest limit is much more useful than confident nonsense.
I would rather look closely at what is here than arrive with the wrong story about it.

contexts.subject: The guide celebrates beating Juan and directs badge-complete trainers toward the League.

SootopolisCity_Gym_1F_Text_GymGuidePostV.text: Yow! You've beaten even JUAN, who\nwas supposedly the best in all HOENN!\pOkay! Check out your TRAINER CARD.\pIf you've gotten all the BADGES, you're\nset for the POKéMON LEAGUE challenge!$

replies.text: Check the card. A whole journey has somehow fitted into eight very small spaces.
We should verify the badges before setting out for the League. Then prepare the whole team.
One important win. The League is another challenge, and we can take time before it.
Seeing all those badges together might feel different from earning the last one.
We should rest, stock up, and let the team enjoy getting this far.
The local finale has opened the door to a much larger final act.
We can be almost there without pretending the road so far was small.
Milestones verified, next objective identified. Now comes the less glamorous supply check.
Eight small signs of all the places that changed us.
I hope you look at the card before hurrying to the next thing you have to prove.
I want to remember this team before the League, exactly as it is now.

contexts.subject: Andrea invites us to see what happens when all ice tiles are cracked.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_AndreaPostBa.text: Watch what happens if you crack all\nthe floor tiles.$

replies.text: That sounded like advice from someone standing safely on the lower floor.
She is inviting an experiment. We should first consider where the floor would send us.
Look at the whole path before stepping. Falling is not the only way to learn.
I would rather understand the pattern before the room makes a loud point about it.
Let us keep everyone steady and take this slowly.
A tempting invitation to let the building deliver its punchline.
The floor has already made its feelings about repeat visitors rather clear.
Each tile changes state. We need a route that accounts for the entire sequence.
The ice remembers each footstep. We should remember them, too.
I prefer a plan to a surprise appointment with the basement.
I am looking at the spaces between our steps as much as the next tile.

contexts.subject: Crissy says we may be strong enough not to lose to Juan in one hit.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_CrissyPostBa.text: You might be good enough to avoid\nbeing wiped out in one hit by JUAN.$

replies.text: We have been promoted from doomed to possibly upright. Wonderful progress.
That is a warning about his power, however faintly the compliment is phrased.
We will prepare properly instead of settling for surviving the first hit.
I think that was encouragement. It had a very small opening to escape through.
Let us make sure the team is rested before testing her estimate.
A glowing forecast of perhaps reaching the second line of dialogue.
A compliment delivered wearing protective gloves.
Surviving one hit is a threshold, not a complete battle plan.
The first wave is only the beginning of the water.
I have received kinder reviews from an ill-fitting mirror.
I would like to know what makes his first attack so dangerous, not merely hear that it is.

contexts.subject: Daphne praises our grace in battle and feels fortunate to have found Pokemon.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_DaphnePostBa.text: The grace you bring to battle is\nfabulous.\pOh… I'm so fortunate to have found\nPOKéMON.$

replies.text: We made someone glad Pokemon exist. That is a rather large compliment for one battle.
She saw something she values in how we battled. I am glad the loss did not hide it.
A strong battle can still be respectful. She noticed.
It is lovely when watching someone else reminds you why you began.
The team helped make that moment. I hope they feel our pride.
An opponent left the scene more in love with the whole enterprise. A wonderful review.
That is so kind I have temporarily forgotten how to stand normally.
Good execution can be satisfying even to the person testing it.
She found beauty in a difficult moment. That is a gift of its own.
Grace is a lovely thing to be noticed for, especially here.
I would like to remember her smile as well as the winning move.

contexts.subject: Connie explains we must walk on each ice tile once to reach Juan.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_ConniePostBa.text: I'll tell you something good.\pIf you want to reach JUAN, you\nneed to walk on each floor tile once.$

replies.text: Each tile once. Finally, a floor with a clear visiting policy.
A route that covers every tile without revisiting one. We should plan before moving.
Good rule to know. Now look at the entire pattern, not just the first few steps.
I want to trace it quietly before my feet have an opinion.
We can take a moment here. Nobody needs to hurry onto cracking ice.
The set requires every square to receive exactly one performance.
Even the floor is enforcing social limits. One visit per tile.
We need a complete path, not a series of locally convenient choices.
Every place asks to be touched once, and then left behind.
Knowing the rule makes the puzzle much less personal.
I am checking the corners first. They may determine how the rest of the route fits.

contexts.subject: Bridget says travelling to train elsewhere would be stronger and more fun than staying in a strong Gym.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_BridgetPostB.text: Rather than being satisfied by being\nin a strong GYM, I imagine training in\lother places will make you stronger.\lBut above all, it looks more fun.$

replies.text: A strong address does not automatically make you strong. Travel does provide better snacks.
A familiar environment can stop testing your assumptions. New opponents help.
She should try it when she is ready. There is more than one place to get stronger.
Wanting to enjoy the road is enough of a reason to see it.
I hope she finds good company as well as good battles.
A supporting character has noticed the road continues past her assigned room.
She is allowed to leave somewhere impressive for somewhere she actually wants to be.
A different environment supplies tests this Gym cannot. Useful, and apparently more appealing.
A sheltered place can still have an open door.
Fun belongs in the plan. It does not make the plan less serious.
I would love to run into her somewhere she chose for herself.

contexts.subject: Olivia sees potential and invites us to stay and train at Juan Gym.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_OliviaPostBa.text: I think you have potential.\nWhy don't you stay and train with us?$

replies.text: A job offer? I am not ready to become a permanent feature of this basement.
She thinks we could learn here. It is a kind offer, not an obligation.
Good to know we would be welcome. The road is still calling us, though.
Being invited to stay feels different from being told to prove we belong.
I like knowing there are places that would make room for us.
Our guest appearance has become an invitation to join the resident cast.
I am touched. I have also grown attached to visiting places with warmer floors.
There would be useful things to learn here. There are useful things ahead, too.
A door opened into a possible life. We can appreciate it without walking through.
She made that offer after seeing us at our best. It sounds sincere.
Maybe we will return for a quieter visit when the next destination is not pulling so hard.

contexts.subject: Tiffany says trainer strength has nothing to do with age.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_TiffanyPostB.text: This is really obvious, but how strong\nyou are as a TRAINER has nothing to do\lwith how young or old you are.$

replies.text: Excellent. I can stop training my birthday and focus on the Pokemon.
Age alone tells us little about preparation, judgment, or the team's particular strengths.
The work matters more than when you were born.
I like being taken seriously without having to become older first.
Different people learn at different times. They still deserve patience.
The calendar has been dismissed from the judging panel.
A welcome policy. I would hate to lose to someone on a clerical technicality.
Review performance, not a convenient proxy for it. Sensible.
A young branch and an old root can both hold their own kind of strength.
It should be obvious. It is still nice when someone actually says it.
I would rather hear about a person's choices than make a story out of their age.

contexts.subject: Bethany wishes she could move past lost causes faster than she can say Oops.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_BethanyPostB.text: I wish I could forget about lost causes\nbefore I can manage an “Oops!”$

replies.text: My Oops has usually finished before my brain has even found the problem.
Recognizing that a plan is failing is a skill. Changing it promptly takes practice.
You can stop a bad plan without turning it into a judgment on yourself.
I know that feeling. My head likes to replay the part I already cannot fix.
A little kindness makes it easier to start the next thing.
She would like her inner editor to work before the entire scene has collapsed.
If she discovers how, I would like to join the waiting list.
Set a point for reevaluating the plan before committing more resources to it.
Some things are ready to be set down before our hands are ready to open.
Moving on quickly is not the only way to move on properly.
I hope she remembers the attempts that taught her something, too.

contexts.subject: Annika joined because Juan praised her Pokemon and wishes she had met him when younger.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_AnnikaPostBa.text: I came to this GYM because JUAN\npraised me for my darling POKéMON.\pOh, if only I'd met JUAN years ago\nwhen I was younger…$

replies.text: One kind remark changed where she wanted to be. That is quite a powerful move.
Feeling recognized can give an old interest a new direction. It is not too late for that.
She is here now. Those years still have something to offer.
I hope she gets to enjoy being seen now, instead of only mourning earlier chances.
Her Pokemon have her, and she has found people who appreciate them. That matters today.
A small compliment became the opening of a much longer chapter.
She did not miss the only version of her life worth having.
The invitation happened now. There are still things she can build from it.
A late-blooming flower still belongs in the garden.
I hope he knows how much that kindness meant to her.
I would ask about her Pokemon first. That seems to be where the happy part began.

contexts.subject: Brianna insists we could not touch Juan despite losing to us.

SootopolisCity_Gym_B1F_Text_BriannaPostB.text: You couldn't lay a finger on JUAN,\nI'm sure. Giggle…$

replies.text: She has promoted our next opponent to a completely untested level of untouchable.
We can take Juan seriously without accepting her forecast as evidence.
We will find out in the battle. No need to win this argument first.
I would rather let the team answer when we get there.
Let us prepare carefully instead of letting that push us into rushing.
The defeated preview insists the main attraction cannot possibly be reviewed.
She sounds certain. Fortunately, certainty does not take a turn in battle.
A claim about another opponent needs a separate test. We are on our way to one.
Her laughter is not a wall. We can keep walking.
I will save my response until we have something more useful than a prediction.
I wonder what she will say when we return. No need to decide it for her yet.

contexts.subject: Juan explains Water Pulse can confuse with ultrasonic waves.

SootopolisCity_Gym_1F_Text_ExplainWaterP.text: The TECHNICAL MACHINE I handed you\ncontains WATER PULSE.\pIn use, it will occasionally confuse\nthe target with ultrasonic waves.\p… … … … … …$

replies.text: Water that makes your thoughts wobble. I had assumed that was just the bath being too hot.
The confusion is a possible added effect, not something to count on every time.
Use it for the attack we can plan around. Treat confusion as a bonus.
It sounds gentle until you imagine being on the other side of it.
We should see which teammate can use it comfortably before teaching it.
A graceful wave with a distinctly ungraceful effect on the opponent's train of thought.
I prefer my confusion self-generated. More predictable supply.
An attack with a secondary disruption effect. We should not build the entire plan on chance.
Still-looking water can carry something we cannot hear.
He made the extra effect clear without promising it would happen every time.
There is more going on in that move than the visible splash.

contexts.subject: Juan directs trainers with all Hoenn badges east to the League on Ever Grande.

SootopolisCity_Gym_1F_Text_JuanPostBattl.text:
The TRAINERS who have gathered all
the GYM BADGES of HOENN should make\lway to the ultimate destination.\pThe POKéMON LEAGUE.\pTravel to the easternmost reaches
of HOENN, to the island EVER GRANDE.\pThere, you shall find the POKéMON
LEAGUE.$

replies.text: Ever Grande. A destination with a name that has very high expectations of itself.
The eastern island is our next major destination. We should prepare before leaving.
Check the route and supplies. Getting there is part of the challenge.
We have talked about the League so long it feels strange to have actual directions.
Let us rest the team before setting off for something this important.
The final destination has acquired a place on the map instead of living only in our speeches.
A big name for a real place we are finally allowed to approach.
Destination identified. Now we need a route and a realistic supply plan.
A far island has become the next step rather than the edge of a dream.
We have earned the invitation. We can still take the time to arrive ready.
I want to remember the team before the crossing, not only after the League.

contexts.subject: Juan imagines us refusing apprenticeship and his coat, then praises that imagined refusal.

SootopolisCity_Gym_1F_Text_JuanPostRemat.text:
JUAN: If I told you to become my
apprentice, you will refuse, I am sure.\pI would like to make a gift of my coat
to you.\pBut again, you will refuse.
I imagine that to be so.\pAnd that, my friend, is a certain sign
of nobility!$

replies.text: He offered a coat, refused it for us, and complimented our answer. I barely had time to want it.
He has constructed a complete exchange without collecting any actual responses.
Generous of him to handle both sides. We appear to have passed.
I might have wanted to see the coat. The conversation moved on without me.
He seems pleased with us. I hope he knows an offer can wait for an answer.
A flawless two-person scene, performed entirely by its most enthusiastic participant.
I enjoy a conversation that lets me contribute absolutely nothing and calls it nobility.
The response was assumed before the offer was tested. Efficient, but not informative.
He has dressed us in an imagined virtue and kept the actual coat.
I would at least like to inspect the coat before my imaginary refusal becomes official.
He looked so pleased with the exchange. I wonder which version of us he was speaking to.

contexts.subject: Brawly compares the depth of battling with the Hoenn sea.

DewfordTown_Gym_Text_BrawlyPostRematch.text: BRAWLY: Battling is vast and it's deep.\nYou can't see the bottom.\lIt's just like the sea of HOENN!$

replies.text: A very deep subject. I am glad the lessons do not all require holding my breath.
Every answer can expose another question. That is part of what keeps study interesting.
There is more to learn. That does not make what we did today small.
I like a familiar thing that can still surprise you after years.
Deep enough to keep learning, wide enough to share with someone.
The sea metaphor has outlasted the match and found a promising second career.
A subject with no bottom. Finally, a respectable home for my overthinking.
A simple set of rules can produce an enormous range of interactions.
We need not reach the bottom to learn how to swim.
I hope he enjoys what he already knows while chasing the next discovery.
I would ask which recent battle surprised him. Even the teacher still has those.

contexts.subject: Brawly welcomes our return but requires two battle-ready Pokemon for the rematch.

DewfordTown_Gym_Text_BrawlyRematchNeedTw.text:
BRAWLY: A wave may draw back, but it
always returns to the shore.\pA giant wave of a talent like you…
I knew you would return!\pOh? You only have one POKéMON
that can battle.\pI'm sorry, but I'd like you to come back
with at least two POKéMON.$

replies.text: The giant wave has returned with a rather small crew. Back to the party list.
He needs two battle-ready Pokemon. We should check health as well as the count.
We need another partner ready to fight. Let us sort that out first.
His welcome was so enthusiastic I briefly forgot we had missed a requirement.
We can return when both teammates are comfortable and ready.
A stirring welcome, followed by the less stirring attendance check.
The wave brought one Pokemon and a disappointing amount of paperwork.
The proposed double battle has one missing participant. Straightforward correction.
Even a returning wave needs enough water to reach the shore.
He is still pleased to see us. We just need to bring the right team.
A warm welcome can survive a second attempt. We will come back prepared.

contexts.subject: Wattson says his team will recharge and welcomes another future challenge.

MauvilleCity_Gym_Text_WattsonPostRematch.text:
WATTSON: We'll have to recharge our
batteries again.\pWhen we're fully charged up, we'll
gladly accept your challenge.\pSo, come back again sometime,
won't you?$

replies.text: Recharging after a battle. I recommend a chair, a snack, and absolutely no wall socket.
Recovery is part of preparation. He sounds happy to make room for it.
Rest the team, then try again. A good plan for both sides.
I like leaving with the feeling we would be welcome back.
Their batteries deserve a proper break. So do ours.
An enthusiastic host announces the interval and immediately books the next performance.
He made resting sound like part of being strong. Good.
A cooling period before another run. Sensible operating procedure.
Even bright things need a quiet place to gather themselves.
I like an invitation that gives everyone time to recover first.
I hope he is still laughing when we return. It makes this place feel like his.

contexts.subject: Wattson realizes we have only one usable Pokemon and asks for at least two.

MauvilleCity_Gym_Text_WattsonRematchNeed.text:
WATTSON: Ah-ha! Here at last!
I know what you want.\lYou want to battle my POKéMON!\pWahahahaha!\pOops! Wait!
You've only one POKéMON with you!\pCome see me with two or more
POKéMON, all right?$

replies.text: He knew what we wanted. Unfortunately, neither of us counted what we brought.
One usable Pokemon is not enough for this format. Check the rest of the party.
We will come back with a proper pair. There is no need to rush it.
The laughter made the mistake feel less terrible. I appreciate that.
Let us heal anyone who needs it before looking for a second teammate.
The joyful reunion has encountered a small casting problem.
I can supply a second opinion. Apparently that does not count.
Two active participants required. We should verify before the next attempt.
The spark is here. We still need another place for it to go.
He managed to correct us without making the whole welcome disappear.
A simple fix. He clearly still wants the battle when we are ready.

contexts.subject: Keegan acknowledges our skill but warns of serious burns against Flannery.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_B1F_Text_KeeganPostBat.text: Your skill is real…\nBut our LEADER FLANNERY is strong.\pIf you don't watch yourself, you'll be\nburned seriously.$

replies.text: A compliment and a burn warning. This Gym has a very consistent welcome package.
He recognizes our skill without dismissing her strength. We should do the same.
Take the warning seriously. Prepare the team before moving on.
I am glad he said we did well before describing the frightening part.
We have time to heal. No badge is worth treating the team carelessly.
Our good review comes with a strongly worded preview of the main attraction.
I would enjoy being complimented more in a room with fewer promised burns.
Known hazard, strong opponent. Check the countermeasures.
A flame deserves care even when we believe we can pass it.
We can respect her power without letting the warning hurry us.
He trains here. It is worth listening when he stops boasting and gives a real warning.

contexts.subject: Jace says our battling spirit may give us a chance against Flannery.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_B1F_Text_JacePostBattl.text: The way the battling spirit burns\nwithin you, you may stand a chance\lagainst our LEADER.$

replies.text: Our spirit is burning. I hope it is the approved metaphorical kind.
Determination helps when it supports careful decisions. We should bring both.
A chance is enough. We will prepare and make the most of it.
It is nice to hear that he saw more than the last attack.
The team has the heart for it. Let us make sure they have the health, too.
An early review has identified a promising spark in the visiting cast.
I can handle a quiet kind of fire. It lasts surprisingly well.
Motivation is available. Next check: resources and matchups.
A small flame can travel far when someone tends it.
He sounds like he wants us to give her a good challenge.
I wonder whether Flannery will recognize the same thing when she sees us.

contexts.subject: Eli stays in the Gym because he admires Flannery power.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_B1F_Text_EliPostBattle.text: I stay here because I became a fan\nof FLANNERY's power.\pHehehehe.$

replies.text: A fan who has chosen the hottest possible seat in the house.
Admiration can be a reason to learn here. I hope he studies the methods as well as the results.
If he wants to train with her, he should take the work seriously.
It is good to be inspired. I hope he finds his own reasons to stay, too.
He seems happy to be here. I hope the team enjoys the training as much.
A devoted audience member has become a permanent part of the venue.
Some fans send letters. This one has committed to the entire thermal environment.
An impressive result should make him curious about how she produced it.
A strong flame can draw people near. They still need a path of their own.
Admiration is fine. She should get to be a person on an ordinary day, too.
I would ask what he has learned from watching her, beyond how strong she is.

contexts.subject: Flannery says she enjoyed the heated rematch despite losing and wants another.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_FlanneryPostRe.text:
FLANNERY: I lost the match,
but I'm completely satisfied.\pIt's not often I get to enjoy a battle
this heated.\pLet's have another one like this
again sometime!$

replies.text: She lost and had a wonderful time. The team should invoice us for entertainment.
A satisfying challenge can be valuable to both sides, regardless of the result.
Good fight, no hard feelings. I would come back for that.
I like how much more like herself she sounds when she is enjoying the battle.
I hope she and her team get a good rest with that happy feeling.
The opponent has requested an encore before the applause has settled.
She does not need to win to feel she belongs here. That is nice to hear.
A useful test and an enjoyable one. Hard to improve on that combination.
The flame burned brightly without leaving bitterness behind.
She sounds comfortable in her own enthusiasm now. It suits her.
I would like to remember that smile when we think back on this Gym.

contexts.subject: Flannery enthusiastically proposes a double rematch then notices only one Pokemon is ready.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_FlanneryRematc.text:
FLANNERY: Losing a battle isn't going
to deflate me.\pI love POKéMON.
I love to battle.\lAnd… I love this GYM!\pLet's exchange superhot moves
in another battle!\pOh, wait. Do you only have one POKéMON
that can battle?\pI hate to say this, but when you come
see me, bring at least two POKéMON.$

replies.text: We brought half a battle to a full-sized welcome.
Her enthusiasm does not change the format. We need two healthy participants.
Another ready teammate first. She will still be here when we return.
She was so excited. I feel bad that our party list interrupted.
Let us take care of whoever cannot battle before trying again.
The fire of anticipation has been briefly contained by a head count.
I have enthusiasm and no battle moves. Apparently a fatal combination for volunteering.
The minimum operating team is two. We currently have one.
A warm invitation can wait while we gather the rest of the team.
She sounds disappointed about the delay, not about us. That helps.
We can give her the rematch she wants once our team is ready for it.

contexts.subject: Winona gives a soaring welcome before noticing the double battle needs another Pokemon.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_WinonaRematchNeedTw.text:
WINONA: We humans can never escape
gravity's pull on the ground.\pBut by striving for excellence,
we have the power to soar!\pYou have scaled the pinnacle as
the reigning CHAMPION.\pPlease, allow me to see your power
at full flight!\pOh, no… Do you have but one
POKéMON with you?\pPlease return with two POKéMON

contexts.subject: Juan welcomes us as a typhoon then asks us to bring two Pokemon for the double rematch.

SootopolisCity_Gym_1F_Text_JuanRematchNe.text:

usual state of serenity…\pBut our young typhoon has returned

contexts.subject: Norman explains parent and child fight fairly but requires two usable Pokemon.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_NormanRematchNeed.text:
DAD: {PLAYER}…
I had a feeling that you would come.\pI would never refuse to accept
a challenge from you.\pYou do understand, don't you?\pInside a GYM, it doesn't matter that
we are a parent and child.\pHm? Wait a second, {PLAYER}.\pDo you only have one POKéMON that is

contexts.subject: Norman sends the inexperienced player to Rustboro and requires four badges before battling.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_NormanGoToRustbor.text:
DAD: Hm? Aren't you going to the

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_NormanGoToDewford.text:
DAD: I see… So, you've beaten
the GYM LEADER in RUSTBORO CITY.\pBut there are many more TRAINERS

contexts.subject: Norman acknowledges the player growing strength from their earned badges.

contexts.subject: Foster admires rocks for hours.

I admire the honesty of this attempt to avoid homework.
Let's identify the mechanism before pressing everything blindly.
A little guidance can leave him with his own discovery.
Help is fine. Becoming his personal button service is less appealing.
I'd ask which buttons he's already tried and what happened.

contexts.subject: Alan wonders how many traps the house contains.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle3_Text_AlanPost.text: I don't get it.\nHow many traps are in this house?\pYou may be the one to solve that.$

replies.text: The answer might be one more than anyone wants.
Counting mechanisms is harder when the route conceals some of them.
Enough to watch our step. That's my count.
I'd rather find the safe way than every single trap.
We should take the route slowly instead of chasing a total.
A house with an extravagant commitment to complications.
I prefer numbers that don't increase beneath my feet.
A map marking each mechanism would turn guesses into evidence.
The house seems fond of keeping one thing out of sight.
The designer clearly believes more is more.
I'd ask which trap has been hardest for him to spot.

contexts.subject: Justin feels trapped among cramped dark doorways.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle3_Text_JustinPo.text: It's full of doors here!\nIt's too small and dark in here! Help!$

replies.text: He needs a way out, not another surprise door.
Let's establish a familiar exit before testing more passages.
Stay with him. Find the way back calmly.
That tight dark space sounds genuinely frightening to him.
We can slow down and help him reach somewhere open.
A distressed guest deserves directions, not more theatrical suspense.
The house has exceeded his recommended daily darkness.
Mark a starting point and check one doorway at a time.
A little clear space may help his breathing settle.
We can stop treating this as entertainment for a moment.
I'd ask which way he entered and walk back with him.

contexts.subject: Martha calls herself weak and directionless.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle3_Text_MarthaPo.text: I know I'm weak!\nAnd, I have no sense of direction!$

replies.text: Two rough moments don't make a complete description of her.
Navigational difficulty and battle results are separate skills to work on.
Needs a route, not another insult from herself.
She sounds frustrated enough to make every problem feel personal.
A calm break and a little help could change the whole afternoon.
An unkind narrator has taken control of her introduction.
Being lost isn't a character flaw. It's common in here.
A simple map could solve one problem immediately.
A tangled place needn't decide what she is capable of.
She can accept help without making herself the joke.
I'd start by asking where she actually wants to go.

contexts.subject: Cora assumes trainers will travel anywhere for a battle.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle4_Text_CoraPost.text: Wouldn't you agree? You would go\nanywhere if TRAINERS were there.$

replies.text: Somewhere in that rule, this house got permission to exist.
Motivation varies. Curiosity can draw people as strongly as competition.
A good battle helps. A safe exit helps too.
Sometimes I just want to see what a strange place is like.
I'd also travel for a good meal. The battle is optional.
A powerful recruitment theory for extremely inconvenient venues.
I reserve the right to avoid certain basements.
Interesting opponents are one reason to explore, not the only one.
Some paths matter for what lies between the challenges.
A place needs more than a guest list to win me over.
I'd ask whether she came for the trainers or the puzzles.

contexts.subject: Paula wonders whether anyone has reached the end.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle4_Text_PaulaPos.text: Has anyone made it to the end?$

replies.text: The end is doing an excellent job of avoiding introductions.
We'd need a completed route or a returning visitor to know.
We'll keep looking. No sense guessing.
It would be reassuring to hear from someone who got through.
A quick rest might make the next attempt less frustrating.
The ending has become the house's most elusive character.
A reasonable question for a building this committed to delay.
Someone could record a confirmed route rather than another rumor.
Not seeing the end yet doesn't mean there isn't one.
I would appreciate an exit with a little more visibility.
I'd ask how far she's managed and compare what we've seen.

contexts.subject: Yuji says puzzles need thought rather than brute force.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle4_Text_YujiPost.text: It's not good enough to be brawny…\nYou have to use your head. Be brainy!$

replies.text: The walls have declined our application to solve them by flexing.
A mechanism rewards understanding of its constraints.
Use your head. Preferably without hitting the wall.
It's nice when stopping to think is the useful move.
A quiet moment can save a lot of wasted effort.
The plot will not advance merely because someone strains impressively.
An argument for thinking that my arms enthusiastically support.
Yes! Figure out the moving parts before applying more force.
A patient look can open what a shove cannot.
Elegance often begins where unnecessary effort stops.
I'd ask what clue changed the way he looked at the room.

contexts.subject: Benny admits trying to cheat contributed to his defeat.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle6_Text_BennyPos.text: Ehehehe… I guess I lost because\nI was trying to cheat.$

replies.text: His shortcut has taken him directly to an awkward explanation.
Cheating also prevented him from testing his actual approach.
Then try it straight next time.
At least he admitted it instead of blaming someone else.
A fair attempt will tell him more about what to practice.
The clever scheme has supplied its own unfavorable ending.
A bad plan with an unusually honest postscript.
A valid attempt gives useful feedback. This one compromised the test.
He can leave the trick behind and begin again plainly.
Owning the mistake is a better look than defending it.
I'd ask what he would try without the shortcut.

contexts.subject: Sebastian wonders if our calm appearance hides a poker face.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle6_Text_Sebastia.text: You don't seem to be affected at all.\nOr do you have your poker face on?$

replies.text: My face often forgets to file the full emotional report.
Outward expression is an imperfect measure of internal response.
Calm face doesn't mean we missed anything.
Sometimes I look quiet because I don't know what to say.
We can be having a busy day without displaying every part.
A composed expression leaves plenty of room for a complicated narrator.
My face isn't a public noticeboard. Usually.
He'd get better information by asking what we noticed.
Still water can hold more than its surface shows.
A reserved look can be natural, not a calculated performance.
I'd tell him what surprised us rather than make him guess.

contexts.subject: Sophia enjoys repeating the Trick House challenge.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle6_Text_SophiaPo.text: I'm sure having a good time checking\nthis place out.\pIt's a challenge I've found worth\nrepeating!$

replies.text: She found a house worth getting confused in twice.
Repeating a challenge can reveal details missed the first time.
Good sign. She likes the work, not just finishing.
Familiar puzzles might feel comfortable in a strange way.
An outing you want to repeat is a good discovery.
A peculiar story with genuine rereading value.
She has formed a surprisingly healthy relationship with frustration.
A second pass is perfect for testing a more efficient route.
A place can stay interesting after it stops being unknown.
Some designs reward another look. This one certainly demands one.
I'd ask what she notices on a return visit that others miss.

contexts.subject: Alexis senses we are solving every Trick House puzzle.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle7_Text_AlexisPo.text: You're solving all the puzzles in the\nTRICK HOUSE. That's the feeling I get.$

replies.text: Our confusion must be looking impressively productive.
She may be noticing the progress our earlier attempts made.
Working on it. One room at a time.
It's nice to hear that we look more certain than I feel.
A little progress at a time still gets us through.
The audience suspects a competent protagonist. How encouraging.
Our stubbornness has been mistaken for a master plan.
Each solved mechanism gives us better clues for the next.
The way can become clearer through walking it carefully.
Apparently our persistence is making a strong impression.
I'd ask what makes her think we're getting them all.

contexts.subject: Alvaro celebrates two odd people meeting in a strange place.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle7_Text_AlvaroPo.text: Well, anyway, we both picked a weird\nplace to get acquainted.\pAs one weirdo to another,\nlet's do our best!$

replies.text: Two weirdos met in a weird house. Very efficient hospitality.
An unusual setting can make an introduction easier to remember.
Strange place. Decent company. Works for me.
It's easier to relax when someone admits this is a little odd.
A friendly person can make a confusing outing worthwhile.
A fine setting for a friendship nobody could call predictable.
A social category I can join without falsifying my application.
Shared curiosity is a perfectly good reason to get acquainted.
A peculiar place has given us an ordinary kindness.
He made being unusual sound welcoming. I like that.
I'd enjoy hearing what drew his particular kind of weird here.

contexts.subject: Everett hoped winning would let him switch places with us.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle7_Text_EverettP.text: I was hoping to switch places with you\nwhen I beat you, but…$

replies.text: He nearly invented a very competitive moving service.
A desired position is not a substitute for understanding the route.
Didn't work. He'll need another way through.
He sounds like he hoped we could solve being stuck for him.
We can explain the path without turning it into a prize.
A positional plot twist defeated by the actual battle.
A complicated way to request a more convenient location.
He might find a direct route once we compare the mechanisms.
A better place can be reached without taking someone else's.
An ambitious shortcut with rather fragile conditions.
I'd ask where he wants to be and what blocks the way.

contexts.subject: Joshua wishes he could appear and vanish like smoke.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle7_Text_JoshuaPo.text: I wish I could appear and disappear as\nif I were smoke, too.$

replies.text: A useful skill for leaving conversations before the awkward part.
Smoke-like movement is an intriguing wish, though rather difficult to reproduce.
Quick exits sound useful. Keep a solid landing.
I'd enjoy being able to leave quietly without anyone staring.
It would make surprise arrivals a little too easy in the kitchen.
An entrance and exit freed from the tyranny of doors.
A social technique I have been trying to master for years.
I'd first ask what effect makes the disappearance look convincing.
A little smoke has inspired a very human wish.
A dramatic silhouette that takes itself away. Stylish.
I'd ask whether he wants the surprise or the freedom most.

contexts.subject: Mariela insists she is not upset.

replies.text: The announcement sounds slightly more upset than advertised.
Her words and tone may not be reporting the same thing.
Fine. No need to press the point.
She can have the feeling without explaining it to us.
A little space might be kinder than trying to catch her out.
An emphatic denial with an exceptionally expressive delivery.
I respect the right to be privately furious in public.
We can let things settle instead of demanding a better report.
A feeling does not need to confess before it can pass.
No need to expose the mood she's trying to cover.
I'd change the subject rather than challenge her expression.

contexts.subject: Patricia blames bad fortune for circling one spot repeatedly.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle7_Text_Patricia.text: I've circled the same spot over ten\ntimes now… It's ill fortune…$

replies.text: That spot has become a very persistent acquaintance.
A repeated route suggests a mechanism or choice pattern worth examining.
Mark the turn. Try something different.
Going around again must make it hard to trust her bearings.
A pause could help before walking the same loop hungry.
The scene has repeated enough times to justify a rewrite.
Ill fortune has suspiciously consistent floor plans.
Track the sequence once. A repeated input may explain the loop.
A familiar circle can open when one small step changes.
Ten visits is enough to call the place a bad habit.
I'd ask which turn she keeps choosing without thinking.

contexts.subject: Keira calls our victory miraculous and permits us to brag.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle8_Text_KeiraPos.text: It's a miracle that you beat me.\nYou can brag about it.$

replies.text: A miracle with official bragging authorization. Very generous.
She found the result surprising enough to frame as exceptional.
No need to brag. The win happened.
I'd rather remember the match than make her hear about it all day.
We can enjoy winning without making her the punchline.
A glowing review delivered in an unusually self-protective wrapper.
I may keep the miracle and decline the announcement.
I'd prefer to know which part of the plan surprised her.
An unexpected result needn't become a public trophy.
Permission accepted. Discretion remains the better accessory.
I'd tell the story with her good moves included too.

contexts.subject: Leroy thinks our progress will please the Trick Master.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle8_Text_LeroyPos.text: Seeing someone like you should please\nthe TRICK MASTER.$

replies.text: The house's owner may be delighted we survived his hospitality.
A designer can learn a great deal from a capable participant.
Good. Maybe he'll provide an uncomplicated exit.
It's nice if our effort means something to the person who built this.
I hope he's as pleased when visitors ask for a rest.
The author may finally meet a reader who survived every footnote.
We have supplied valuable data about confusing stubborn people.
I'd love to compare the intended solution with what we actually did.
A strange creation has found someone willing to follow its path.
A good design should welcome people who really engage with it.
I'd ask what reaction the Trick Master usually hopes to see.

contexts.subject: Vincent is astonished we defeated the League Champion.

Route110_TrickHousePuzzle8_Text_VincentP.text: You've beaten the POKéMON LEAGUE\nCHAMPION? That's too much!$

replies.text: That title does tend to make an introduction rather large.
A major victory can change how someone interprets a later battle.
Still the same trainer standing here.
It's a big thing to hear said aloud in this odd little room.
There was a lot of ordinary care behind that extraordinary day.
A rather significant chapter has entered this peculiar conversation.
An intimidating credential, currently wandering through a puzzle house.
Even that achievement came from solving one problem at a time.
A great moment can travel quietly with the person who lived it.
A grand reputation doesn't stop us getting dusty like everyone else.
I'd rather tell him about the match than just repeat the title.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt claims the boss knows everything while admitting ignorance.

Route119_WeatherInstitute_1F_Text_Grunt1.text: Our BOSS knows everything.\pBut I'm just a GRUNT. What would I know\nabout what he's thinking?$

replies.text: A very confident organization with a remarkably uninformed spokesperson.
His certainty about the boss exceeds the evidence he can explain.
Doesn't know the plan. Still chose to help.
He sounds less certain once he talks about his own part.
Not knowing doesn't erase what he's doing to the people here.
An omniscient leader, according to a narrator with no information.
A blank page defending the brilliance of the whole book.
Blind confidence is a poor substitute for understanding the objective.
Obedience can move a hand without answering its conscience.
That defense has impressive posture and very little substance.
I'd pay attention to what he actually did, not his praise of the boss.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt fears reprimand and wants a nap in an Institute bed.

Route119_WeatherInstitute_1F_Text_Grunt4.text: Oh, no…\nI'll catch an earful for losing to a kid…\pI should just take a nap in the bed…$

replies.text: His plan has gone from taking over to taking a nap.
Fear of reprimand doesn't justify using someone else's workplace as a refuge.
Leave the staff's beds alone. Go.

Those beds are for people who belong here and need rest.
A failed invasion has developed an interest in the guest facilities.
The audacity is almost restful in its consistency.
Withdrawal would be a better next step than settling in.
His discomfort does not outrank the lives he interrupted.
An unwelcome guest shouldn't start reviewing the bedding.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt wants the Institute's weather-changing Pokemon.

Route119_WeatherInstitute_2F_Text_Grunt2.text: If the POKéMON they made here can\ncontrol the weather freely, then we of\lTEAM AQUA definitely need it!$

replies.text: He heard remarkable Pokemon and immediately skipped to stealing.
A Pokemon's unusual capability doesn't entitle them to control it.

The Pokemon deserves care, not a place in their scheme.
A living creature reduced to a convenient device in their plot.

A life is not a prize for whoever wants it most loudly.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt angrily says we do not understand their goals.

Route119_WeatherInstitute_2F_Text_Grunt3.text: You don't have any idea what we of\nTEAM AQUA are working towards!\lYou stay out of our way!$

replies.text: A secret plan is apparently also an excuse to be rude.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt cryptically insists their real objective is elsewhere.

Route119_WeatherInstitute_2F_Text_Grunt5.text: Humph, so what?\nWhat we want…\pWhat we really want isn't here…\nIhihihihi…$

contexts.subject: Hugo declares that life is about Pokemon and playing games.

contexts.subject: Jasper insists a Pokemon trainer cannot be a coward.

Route24_Text_ReliPostBattle.text: I did my best, so I've no regrets!$

Route24_Text_TimmyPostBattle.text: I did my best. I have no regrets!$

replies.text: A loss with a clean landing. They know they showed up properly.

contexts.subject: Braxton urges us to spread the word about conserving energy.

contexts.subject: Dillon asks to be left alone after the battle.

contexts.subject: Dirk dismisses our victory as luck.

contexts.subject: Yasu wonders about the strength of a large Pokemon descending from the mountains.

contexts.subject: Bernie ends his break and returns to work.

It is nice to see a little of the rest of someone's day.

An adventure can fit between two ordinary pieces of work.

contexts.subject: Dave decides he needs to catch stronger Pokemon.

contexts.subject: Ned has snagged his fishing line.

contexts.subject: Chip thinks a better fishing rod would broaden his catches.

contexts.subject: Luca recommends Electric attacks against sea Pokemon.

contexts.subject: Hank accepts our battle skill but boasts that he is still the better angler.

Route12_Text_HankPostBattle.text: I guess you get to be good at\nwhat you like.\pWell, you beat me at POKéMON,\nbut you can't top me at fishing.$

replies.text: He has saved one crown and graciously lent us the other.
Different activities reward different practice. One result does not rank every skill.
Fair enough. He knows what he is good at.
It is nice that losing did not make him forget what he enjoys.
We do not all need to be best at the same thing.
A diplomatic settlement: the field is ours, the fishing platform remains his.
A loss leaves plenty of room for another kind of pride.
Separate skill sets, separate rankings. Reasonable enough.
He has another quiet place where he knows his own hands.
A little boast, but he gave the team credit first.
I would be curious to watch him fish after hearing that confidence.

contexts.subject: Elliot says losing no longer bothers him.

Route12_Text_ElliotPostBattle.text: It's all right.\nLosing doesn't bug me anymore.$

replies.text: He has made peace with the scoreboard. Saves a lot of grumbling.
Accepting a result can make it easier to examine without defensiveness.
Good. Plenty left to enjoy after one loss.
I hope that means he can enjoy the battle more easily now.
A calmer ending is good for the whole team.
The defeat has been admitted without being given the whole room.
Some disappointments get smaller once you stop feeding them.
Less frustration leaves more room to learn from the result.
The water keeps moving, and he seems ready to move with it.
There is a relaxed confidence in not needing every result to flatter you.
I wonder what changed his mind about losing.

contexts.subject: Andrew complains that the Magikarp he catches are weak.

Route12_Text_AndrewPostBattle.text: What, MAGIKARP?\pI catch them all the time, sure.\nBut, boy are they wimpy.$

replies.text: They are doing their best at being Magikarp. A demanding profession.
A Pokemon's current battle performance does not exhaust its possible value.
If he keeps catching them, he could at least treat them with respect.
It sounds unkind when the Pokemon did nothing but be caught.
A little patience can matter more than calling a partner useless.
The angler's abundant supporting cast has received a rather ungrateful review.
Poor fish. Being common apparently earns them extra criticism.
Repeatedly getting the same result suggests reviewing the method, not insulting the output.
A small fish still has a whole life behind its small splash.
He could want a different catch without putting these ones down.
I wonder whether he knows anything about them beyond their battle strength.

contexts.subject: Jes dramatically asks Gia to forgive his role in their defeat.

Route12_Text_JesPostBattle.text: JES: Oh, GIA, forgive me,\nmy love!$

replies.text: That is a lot of apology for one battle. I hope he remembers to breathe.
Taking responsibility is useful; assuming the entire result was his fault may not be.
Apologize once, then work out what actually went wrong.
He seems more frightened of disappointing Gia than of losing.
A calmer conversation would probably help them both more.
A roadside tragedy in which the stakes may need a slightly smaller orchestra.
The apology has arrived before the practical review. By quite a distance.
Emotional alarm is high. Troubleshooting would work better at a lower volume.
He is trying to mend something before knowing where it broke.
He cares what she thinks. I hope he can hear his own thoughts too.
I wonder whether they usually talk this way after a loss.

contexts.subject: Gia blames Jes for spoiling their double battle.

Route12_Text_GiaPostBattle.text: GIA: JES, you silly!\nYou ruined this!$

replies.text: A team of two should not become a blame delivery service.
Assigning fault before reviewing their joint choices is unlikely to improve coordination.
They both battled. They both need a fair say afterward.
That sounds harsh when he is already apologizing.
A kind word would do more for the next attempt than another sharp one.
The partnership's post-match review has become regrettably one-sided.
Disappointment does not need a person to stand in front of it and take the hit.
Blame is not the same as a useful diagnosis.
A shared defeat should not leave only one person standing in the cold.
She can be upset without making him the whole problem.
I wonder what he would say if he felt able to answer honestly.

contexts.subject: Kindra explains that only the original trainer can change a traded Pokemon's nickname.

Route15_Text_KindraPostBattle.text: You can't change the nickname of\nany POKéMON you get in a trade.\pOnly the Original TRAINER can get\nthe nickname changed.$

replies.text: A name can travel farther than the person who chose it.
The nickname retains a link to the original trainer through that restriction.
Best know that before agreeing to a trade.
A familiar name may matter to the Pokemon even when its home changes.
Worth considering the name as part of the partner you are welcoming.
A former trainer's creative decision has acquired remarkable permanence.
A little piece of the old life arrives with the new companion.
Persistent naming rights. Important constraint to know in advance.
Someone's first word for you can follow a long journey.
A nickname carries taste and history. Sometimes more of one than the other.
I wonder what memorable traded name made her bring that up.

contexts.subject: Becky says the Bikers' appearance frightens her.

Route15_Text_BeckyPostBattle.text: I'm afraid of BIKERS. They look so\nugly and mean!$

replies.text: Looking mean is not proof. Acting mean would be a more convincing clue.
Appearance alone is an unreliable predictor of how someone will behave.
Keep space if you feel unsafe. Judge what people actually do.
I understand being nervous, though looks do not tell the whole story.
She deserves to feel safe without deciding every stranger is dangerous.
A costume has received a moral review before the wearer has spoken.
Dark clothes attract a surprising amount of fictional wrongdoing.
Visual warning signs can be misleading. Actual behavior is better evidence.
A sharp outline does not always hide a sharp intention.
Some people cultivate a rough look. That still leaves the person to meet.
I wonder whether someone frightened her or she has only seen them from afar.

contexts.subject: Edwin doubts he is suited to battling after losing.

Route15_Text_EdwinPostBattle.text: Maybe I'm not cut out for battles.\nI'm not the right type, I guess.$

replies.text: One loss is a very small audition for a whole life.
A single result cannot establish whether he could improve with suitable practice.
He can decide later. No need to write himself off while it still stings.
I know how quickly one bad attempt can sound like a final answer.
There are other ways to enjoy Pokemon if battles do not make him happy.
A disappointing scene need not decide the casting of the whole story.
Perhaps he needs a different approach. Perhaps a different joy. Neither is failure.
One test is not a complete assessment of capability.
A path can be difficult without being closed to you.
He is allowed to keep trying, and allowed to prefer something else.
I wonder whether he enjoyed any part of the battle before judging himself.

contexts.subject: Chester explains that Ground attacks such as Earthquake and Fissure do not affect birds.

Route15_Text_ChesterPostBattle.text: This is so obvious, you should know\nthis, but…\pMoves like EARTHQUAKE and FISSURE\nhave no effect on bird POKéMON.$

replies.text: Hard to shake the ground under someone who is not standing on it.
Flying immunity is an important matchup consideration for Ground attacks.
Check what the opponent can ignore before choosing a move.
Useful advice, though he did not need to make knowing it sound mandatory.
A reminder can help even when somebody thinks the rule is obvious.
The lesson is useful; the little preface announcing its obviousness less so.
The earth may complain all it likes. A flying bird need not answer.
A powerful tool is useless against the wrong target. Always check compatibility.
The ground cannot catch every creature that passes above it.
He could share that without making someone feel foolish for learning it now.
I wonder how many trainers he has seen try the wrong move here.

contexts.subject: Grace says she forgives our victory and is old enough to cope.

Route15_Text_GracePostBattle.text: I forgive you.\nI can take it.\lI'm a big girl now.$

replies.text: She has granted us absolution for following the battle rules. Very generous.
She seems to be reassuring herself that she can manage disappointment.
She held up fine. A loss is allowed to sting a little.
Trying to sound grown-up after something hurts is very familiar.
She can be proud of trying without pretending she felt nothing.
A dignified pardon, issued while its author steadies herself.
Growing up need not mean becoming impossible to upset.
Handling a setback is a skill. This looks like practice.
A small voice can stand a little taller after being shaken.
She is giving herself a way to leave with her head up.
I wonder whether saying it aloud helped her believe it.

contexts.subject: Olivia treasures her Pokemon greeting her when she gets home.

Route15_Text_OliviaPostBattle.text: I love having my POKéMON greet me\nwhen I get home.\pIt's so reassuring.$

replies.text: A welcoming committee with tails. Extremely strong argument for going home.
A familiar greeting can make returning home reliably comforting.
Good to have somebody glad you made it back.
I can hear the warmth in how she talks about that moment.
That sounds like the best part of an ordinary evening.
No grand ceremony can quite compete with being expected by someone delighted.
A little proof that your absence was noticed kindly.
Reliable positive feedback at the door. Hard to improve that design.
A house feels different when something inside is listening for you.
Being welcomed without needing to impress anyone is a lovely luxury.
I wonder which one always gets to the door first.

contexts.subject: Ernest glorifies outlaw life and cheers for Team Rocket.

Route15_Text_ErnestPostBattle.text: Life's too short.\nIt's cool to live as an outlaw.\lTEAM ROCKET RULES!$

replies.text: Life is short. Making everyone else's day worse is a strange way to spend it.
Excitement does not justify harming others. The slogan offers no actual defense.
People get hurt by that crowd. Nothing cool about it.
He sounds excited by the image and uninterested in who suffers for it.
There are better ways to feel alive than frightening people.
A glamorous outlaw fantasy has omitted every person left to clean up afterward.
Cruelty in an interesting jacket is still cruelty.
If the plan requires ignoring the damage, the plan is bad.
A short life is no reason to leave sharp pieces in other people's paths.
A rough image does not make hurting people stylish.
I wonder whether he has ever listened to someone Team Rocket actually frightened.

contexts.subject: Alex dismisses his earlier demand for money as a joke.

Route15_Text_AlexPostBattle.text: I was just joking about the money.\nDon't take me all serious.$

replies.text: An odd joke if only the person asking for money knows it is funny.
Calling a demand a joke afterward does not remove its effect at the time.
Then pick a joke that does not sound like a threat.
It did not feel especially lighthearted from this side.
A joke works better when the other person can relax enough to laugh.
The threatening opening has received a hasty comic rewrite.
A convenient punchline, arriving just after the consequence.
Intent should be clearer before someone else has to assess the risk.
Some words leave a bruise even after someone calls them light.
He could acknowledge how it sounded instead of blaming us for hearing it.
I wonder whether he says that every time someone objects.

contexts.subject: Celia says she frequently trades Pokemon with friends.

Route15_Text_CeliaPostBattle.text: I trade POKéMON with my friends\nall the time.$

replies.text: Her Pokemon have a very well-connected social circle.
Regular trades between friends could expose everyone to a wider range of partners.
Good to know the people you are trusting with a partner.
It must be nice to keep hearing how the Pokemon are doing afterward.
Friends can make the change feel a little less uncertain.
A lively exchange network, with friendship doing the paperwork.
A new home does not have to mean every familiar door closes.
A trusted exchange network! Much less guesswork than dealing with strangers.
The roads between friends carry more than the friends themselves.
Knowing one another's tastes probably makes the choices easier.
I wonder whether their Pokemon recognize one another when the friends meet up.

contexts.subject: Yazmin decides to practice against weaker opponents.

Route15_Text_YazminPostBattle.text: I'll go train with weaker people.$

replies.text: A gentler challenge can help. Just do not mistake easy wins for the whole lesson.
Appropriate difficulty can support practice, provided the goal is skill rather than reassurance.
Train at a workable level. Do not bully somebody smaller.
It is reasonable to want a challenge she can understand better.
A steady next step can help more than repeating an overwhelming fight.
A smaller stage may help her rehearse, if applause is not the only objective.
There is a difference between finding your pace and finding someone to crush.
Reduce difficulty, isolate the skill, then increase it again. Good if done deliberately.
A shallow place can teach you to stand before you try the deep water.
Useful practice should build confidence without borrowing it from someone else's humiliation.
I wonder what specific part of her battling she wants to improve.

contexts.subject: Mya plans to add to the siblings' training schedule after losing.

Route15_Text_MyaPostBattle.text: MYA: Okay, we'll turn it up.\nI'll add to our training menu!$

replies.text: The training menu has expanded. I hope rest is still one of the courses.
More practice can help if it addresses what actually happened in this match.
Ask her partner how much they can handle before adding more.
She is eager to improve. I hope they agree on what the new plan looks like.
A sensible menu includes recovery as well as hard work.
The schedule has grown in response to criticism from reality.
More is an easy answer. Better takes a little more thought.
Add the exercise that fixes the problem, not simply more of everything.
A growing plan still needs room for people to breathe inside it.
Enthusiasm is good. Making a plan together would be better.
I wonder whether Ron helped choose anything on that menu.

contexts.subject: Ron wishes his sister were nicer after she increases their training.

Route15_Text_RonPostBattle.text: RON: Oh, bleah…\nI wish I had a nice sister…$

replies.text: The revised training menu has received a complaint from the dining room.
His reaction suggests the new schedule needs more discussion between them.
He should get a say in the training he has to do.
He sounds worn down more than excited about improving.
They might enjoy practicing more if they planned it together.
The supporting sibling would like a word with the author of the schedule.
A family team still needs room for both people's wishes.
Poor agreement at the planning stage becomes poor morale during the work.
A shared road feels longer when only one person chooses the pace.
A little kindness would probably get further than another added drill.
I wonder whether she hears how unhappy he sounds.

contexts.subject: Lao defensively says the group likes spending time here.

Route16_Text_LaoPostBattle.text: We like just hanging here.\nWhat's it to you?$

replies.text: A simple answer wearing a rather spiky coat.
Enjoying the location is an adequate reason to be here. The hostility adds little.
He can stay. We can pass. Easy arrangement.
I do not mind where he spends his afternoon.
There is room to enjoy the place without making visitors feel unwelcome.
The local leisure committee has issued a defensive statement.
Standing somewhere need not become a declaration of war.
Compatible requirements: they stay here, we continue down the road.
A familiar patch of ground can matter a great deal to someone.
He sounds ready for an argument nobody needs to start.
I wonder what they like most about this particular spot.

contexts.subject: Koji angrily denies needing our bicycle after losing.

Route16_Text_KojiPostBattle.text: Forget it, who needs your BIKE!$

replies.text: The bicycle has survived a very moody appraisal.
The change of attitude appears more related to the result than the bicycle.
Good. Our bike stays right here with us.
That sounds like a conversation best left finished.
No argument needed. We can keep moving.
The coveted object has abruptly lost all appeal in the official account.
A remarkably convenient change of taste.
Ownership dispute canceled. Excellent outcome for the bicycle.
The road remains open, and the bike remains ours.
He has decided it was never desirable. A familiar recovery strategy.
I wonder how long this new lack of interest will last.

contexts.subject: Luke angrily says he hates losing and tells us to leave.

Route16_Text_LukePostBattle.text: I hate losing!\nGet out of my face!$

replies.text: He has had enough of the result and quite enough of us. Time to go.
Disappointment is understandable. The hostile delivery is still unnecessary.
Leave him space. Nothing to gain by staying.
I would rather go before he finds something else to be angry about.
A quiet break would help him more than another exchange.
A frank critical assessment of losing, followed by an eviction notice.
An unpleasant feeling has become an unpleasant conversation. We can stop one of those.
Overheated system. Best give it room to cool down.
Let the sharp feeling spend itself without standing in its way.
He could be more gracious. We can still be sensible about leaving.
I wonder whether his team gets a kinder response once the visitors leave.

contexts.subject: Hideo insists the group will stay and suggests the coastal detour between Fuchsia and Vermilion.

Route16_Text_HideoPostBattle.text: We'll always be hanging around here\neven if you don't like it.\pYou can detour to VERMILION from\nFUCHSIA going along the coast.$

replies.text: A stubborn declaration with travel advice attached. Unexpectedly useful.
The coastal route is useful information, though it may be a considerable detour.
We can use the road without asking them to move away.
He seems determined to argue. I appreciate the directions more than the tone.
A detour is an option, but we should know how much farther it takes us.
An entrenched resident briefly moonlights as a coastal travel adviser.
A prickly conversation has left one practical thing on the table.
Alternative route supplied. Need to compare distance and conditions before choosing.
Even a difficult voice can point toward a useful road.
He gave us a direction while insisting he does not care. Interesting combination.
I wonder whether he has taken that coastal route himself.

contexts.subject: Camron wants ferocious Pokemon to injure his enemies.

Route16_Text_CamronPostBattle.text: If I'm going to have POKéMON, they\nmay as well be ferocious.\pI'd use them to leave my enemies\nin tatters.$

replies.text: That is a lot of ugly intention to put on a Pokemon's shoulders.
He is describing deliberate harm, not ordinary competitive training.
Pokemon are partners. They are not his excuse to hurt people.
I do not want to stay close to someone talking like that.
He is asking living creatures to carry his grudges for him.
A menacing image has become a frankly unpleasant plan.
Cruelty does not improve when somebody else does the biting for you.
That goal is the problem. Better equipment would only make it worse.
A creature should not be made into the sharp edge of someone's spite.
He can keep that fantasy. We should keep our distance.
I wonder how his Pokemon are treated when they do not seem fierce enough.

contexts.subject: Ruben brags about using his Pokemon to frighten and bite people.

Route16_Text_RubenPostBattle.text: I get my kicks by harassing people\nwith my stinking POKéMON.\pThey're great for startling people.\nAnd, they bite, too.$

replies.text: His idea of fun keeps arriving at somebody else's expense.
He is deliberately encouraging harmful behavior toward passersby.
Keep the team close. We are not giving him another opportunity.
That sounds frightening for anyone who simply wants to use the road.
Scaring people and getting them bitten is a rotten use of a partner's trust.
The boast contains no redeeming twist. Just a bully enjoying an audience.
An ugly little hobby. I am comfortable leaving him disappointed in our reaction.
The dangerous part is that he considers this a successful outcome.
Some people leave teeth in the memory of an ordinary walk.
If the joke needs an unwilling victim, the joke is doing poorly.
I wonder how many travelers have changed routes because of him.

contexts.subject: Jed asks Lea to pay less attention to him during battles.

Route16_Text_JedPostBattle.text: JED: Listen, LEA.\nYou need to focus less on me.$

replies.text: A flattering distraction is still a distraction when the other team is attacking.
Divided attention can interfere with coordination, even when the reason is affectionate.
Fair request. Watch the battle while you are in it.
That must be an awkward thing to say while somebody is smiling at you.
They might have more fun if both can stay involved in the actual match.
The romantic subplot has been asked to stop blocking the main action.
Admiration has developed a minor tactical disadvantage.
Attention allocation problem. He has identified it fairly clearly.
Even a fond gaze can face the wrong direction for a moment.
He asked directly rather than making her guess. Good start.
I wonder whether she realizes how much of the match she missed.

contexts.subject: Lea apologizes for being distracted by her admiration for Jed.

Route16_Text_LeaPostBattle.text: LEA: Ehehe, I'm sorry.\nJED is so cool.$

replies.text: She heard the complaint. The admiration remains fully operational.
She acknowledges the distraction without appearing particularly discouraged.
Save the staring for after the match. Everybody wins.
She seems happy enough to admit exactly what happened.
A little focus during battle leaves plenty of time to enjoy each other's company later.
The romantic subplot apologizes while firmly retaining its leading man.
An embarrassingly happy explanation. There are worse problems to have.
Cause confirmed. Now they need an actual adjustment, not just a cheerful diagnosis.
Her thoughts keep wandering toward a very familiar face.
She is not even pretending to have a more dignified excuse. Fair enough.
I wonder whether Jed is trying not to look pleased.

contexts.subject: Wilton wishes he owned a bicycle.

Route18_Text_WiltonPostBattle.text: I wish I had a BIKE!$

replies.text: A road full of bicycles is a very persistent advertisement.
The nearby cycling route makes that wish especially understandable.
Would make some of these long stretches easier.
Watching everyone ride past must make the walk feel longer.
A good bike can turn an errand into something you look forward to.
The scenery has supplied a repeated demonstration of the thing he lacks.
Envy with wheels. At least it has a practical use.
Human-powered transport is satisfying when the road cooperates.
Two small circles can make the world feel less far away.
He knows exactly which purchase would improve his afternoons.
I wonder where he would ride first if he got one.

contexts.subject: Ramiro enjoys collecting sea Pokemon on weekends because the coast is nearby.

Route18_Text_RamiroPostBattle.text: I collect sea POKéMON on weekends\nbecause the sea is so close.$

replies.text: A local sea and a weekend plan. Nicely organized happiness.
A nearby habitat makes repeated observation and practice much easier.
Good to make use of a place he knows well.
It is nice to have something familiar to look forward to.
A regular day outside can do a lot for a long working week.
The weekend has a reliable coastal appointment.
An ordinary shoreline becomes a private little reason to anticipate Saturday.
Convenient access makes a hobby much easier to keep doing.
The sea is close enough to become part of his week.
He has built a pleasant routine around what is already nearby.
I wonder whether the same shore still surprises him after so many visits.

contexts.subject: Jacob calls this his favorite Pokemon-catching area.

Route18_Text_JacobPostBattle.text: This is my fave area for catching\nPOKéMON.$

replies.text: He has a favorite patch of the map. Those are good to collect too.
Repeated visits could give him detailed knowledge of the local encounters.
Knowing a place well can be worth more than rushing somewhere new.
A favorite place makes an ordinary outing feel easier to begin.
Nice to find somewhere that keeps giving you reasons to come back.
A familiar stretch of ground has earned a standing recommendation.
He has found somewhere that does not wear out when repeated.
Local expertise! He probably notices changes a visitor would miss.
A place can become yours without belonging to you.
A clear favorite, with no need to make it sound fashionable.
I wonder what keeps drawing him back to this particular area.

contexts.subject: Barry wishes he could ride a Pokemon rather than swim.

Route20_Text_BarryPostBattle.text: I wish I could ride my POKéMON.\nI bet you're not tired.$

replies.text: He has spotted the difference between a sea trip and an arm workout.
Swimming and riding make very different demands on the traveler.
Tired? Stop somewhere safe before it becomes trouble.
I can understand envying a comfortable ride from down in the water.
A rest would help more than comparing how tired everyone looks.
Our transport has received an envious review from a floating critic.
The view is probably lovelier when you are not swallowing it.
A good transport method reduces the work. Someone still has to do it.
The sea feels bigger when your own arms have to measure it.
He is noticing comfort at exactly the point he could use some.
I wonder how much farther he intended to swim today.

contexts.subject: Shirley tells us a huge cavern lies beneath the island.

Route20_Text_ShirleyPostBattle.text: There's a huge cavern underneath\nthis island.$

replies.text: An island with a whole downstairs. The sea keeps surprisingly large secrets.
The visible island may be only a small part of the geological structure.
Good to know. A cavern near the sea deserves careful footing.
It is strange to stand above so much empty space.
Exploring somewhere like that takes preparation, not just curiosity.
A modest island turns out to have a considerably larger interior life.
A dark room beneath all this brightness. Rather appealing.
A huge underground space! I wonder how water moves through it.
The land has kept a hollow thought beneath the waves.
That changes how I imagine the little bit we can see.
I wonder how much of the cavern she has actually explored.

contexts.subject: Tiffany invites us to float with her.

replies.text: For once, an invitation that does not involve going anywhere at all.
A quiet pause can be appealing, provided the water and current are safe.
Only if the conditions are safe. The sea can move you without asking.
That sounds peaceful. A little quiet company without much conversation.
A gentle break could be nice when everyone knows their limits.
An admirably minimalist outing: remain here, and let the water do the staging.
Being quietly beside someone can be enough of a plan.
Low-effort recreation, variable drift. Keep an eye on the shore.
A little while held up by something larger than yourself.
A relaxed invitation. She makes stopping feel like a proper activity.
I wonder whether she has a favorite spot where the water stays calm.

contexts.subject: Irene says Seafoam was once one island.

Route20_Text_IrenePostBattle.text: SEAFOAM used to be a single island\nin the distant past.$

replies.text: The islands used to be one? Even the map has old family stories.
Coastal erosion and geological change can transform a landmass over time.
The sea has been working on this place longer than any of us.
It is difficult to imagine the gap between them filled with land.
A reminder that familiar places have histories far older than ours.
The landscape has undergone an extensive revision since its first edition.
Two pieces of land remembering a shape nobody living saw.
A changed structure leaves clues. I would look for matching layers of rock.
The water now lives where the island once held hands with itself.
That makes the gap feel like part of the place's story.
I wonder what evidence first showed people they used to be connected.

contexts.subject: Dean realizes he trained his own physique while neglecting his Pokemon's preparation.

Route20_Text_DeanPostBattle.text: I should've been buffing up my\nPOKéMON, not me!$

replies.text: The muscles attended the workout. The battle team apparently missed the invitation.
His personal fitness does not substitute for preparing the partners doing the battling.
Training the team is his job too. Good that he noticed.
It is useful to see the gap instead of just being angry about losing.
He can keep enjoying his exercise and still make time for the Pokemon.
The leading physique has discovered that the supporting cast needs rehearsal.
An impressive silhouette cannot do everyone else's homework.
Optimized the wrong subsystem. Familiar mistake, honestly.
Strength in one place does not fill every empty place beside it.
At least his conclusion includes something he can change.
I wonder how he will include the team in his next training day.

contexts.subject: Darrin thinks riding a Pokemon over the sea looks fun.

Route20_Text_DarrinPostBattle.text: Riding a POKéMON sure looks fun!$
